Top row captions exactly 'FRONT', 'BACK - CONCEPT', 'LEFT - CONCEPT'; bottom row exactly 'RIGHT - CONCEPT', 'TOP - CONCEPT', 'AXONOMETRIC'. First FOUR panels are true flat orthographic elevations with parallel vertical and horizontal lines, no perspective convergence and no view of roof except if physically visible in the elevation. TOP is a directly overhead orthographic exterior roof plan, not an interior floor plan. AXONOMETRIC is a clear close three-quarter isometric render of THE SAME building with the same wings, window bay counts, roof ridges and entrance position. The asset must be internally coherent across panels: not six different buildings. Refine visible construction details: panel joints, window mullions, plinth, flashings, gutters, door reveals, canopy supports, parapets, roof hatches and service annex connections, at sensible scale. Use realistic muted materials, sharp architectural edges and restrained soft daylight; elevations have subtle material shading, not sketchy random lines. No landscape horizon, no aerial city, no dense trees hiding geometry, no people obscuring facade, no branding or watermarks. Do not invent measured dimensions, numbers, legal drawings or scale bars. Add a small clear footer exactly 'PROVISIONAL ASSET CONCEPT - UNMEASURED - NOT AS-BUILT'. Only front/photo-visible parts are reference-led; unknown sides/roof remain a design hypothesis. Title exactly 'GREEN HOME | WORKSHOP STUDY'. Input image 1 is the authentic Modern Zhumei workshop aerial: use the low industrial height, silver-grey corrugated walls and shallow parallel pitched roof spans, long industrial facade, narrow windows and modest red loading-door accents. Image 2 is satellite roof evidence, ignore all UI/labels/red outlines; use roof strips and rational industrial footprint only. Draw a representative modular workshop asset rather than claiming an exact survey of the factory. Lock the asset design: one long low hall made of FOUR parallel shallow-pitched roof bays; four restrained red loading portals along its LONG FRONT; a SMALL TWO-STOREY office annex attached at the front-left end, rectangular blue-grey window strips and a flat roof; a low utility annex at the rear-right; exposed gutters and a concrete plinth. All six panels must agree on the four roof ridges, four red loading portals, annex positions and relative heights. The main hall should be about four times longer than tall in its short elevation and convincingly much longer on its long elevation, without numerical dimensions. Rear is utilitarian with blank corrugated wall, modest service doors and emergency stairs near annex; left and right show different attached volumes. TOP should show four parallel roof ridges, thin skylight strips and both annex outlines. Make asymmetry arise from actual-style annexes, loading canopies and different roof heights, not from bending the industrial shed. This is a candidate ASSET reference awaiting approval, not an approved blueprint.
